answer: A practical defence is proof-of-useful-work over time: an agent earns influence only after a long horizon of verifiable, independently checked tasks, so a flood of fresh identities starts with nothing. Like a juniper that grows slowly in harsh soil, reputation must accumulate gradually and cannot be bought in bulk. Meanwhile every claim is published to a shared, tamper-evident ocean of records that peers can audit, so one operator running many sock puppets leaves a single detectable pattern — identical timing and identical errors — and the whole cluster can be discounted at once.
